method: Re-fetch 300 products for 'brake pads for 2018 Honda Civic Si' with correct pagination. Print product.id and variants[].seller.domain side by side. Compare with U8-A data.
rootCause: The U8-A script (probe-u8a-refined.ts) used `--set '/query=...,cursor=...'` (comma-separated) instead of separate `--set '/query=...' --set '/pagination/cursor=...'` arguments. This put the cursor into the query string, breaking pagination. The API returned the first ~10 products repeatedly, giving 16 distinct IDs instead of the real ~248.
verdict: REGISTER ENTRY 1 IS CORRECT. The Catalog returns per-merchant rows, not UPID clusters. Each product row has exactly 1 variant with 1 seller. The same physical part appears as separate rows with different product IDs, one per merchant. The §3 finding of '16 distinct products' is WRONG — it is an artifact of broken pagination in the U8-A script.
consequences: Register entry 1 stands. H5 (offer attachment) remains killed — the response shape does not contain clusters.
The §3 '16 distinct products' reframe is withdrawn. The ~300 set contains ~248 distinct product IDs, each from a single seller.
The 'controlled comparison' from §3 (PRL intake appearing 30x, Subimods absent) is also withdrawn — the 30x repetition was an artifact of broken pagination.

The World B finding (stable set with noisy ordering, Jaccard 0.90-1.00) needs re-validation with correct pagination. The high Jaccard was measuring overlap of the same 10-16 products across runs, not 300 distinct products.
The 'listings vs products' distinction from §3 is moot — 300 rows are ~248 distinct products from ~248 distinct merchants, not 16 products repeated from 30 merchants each.
